title: Approximating Memorization Using Loss Surface Geometry for Dataset Pruning and Summarization

problem.claim: Sustainable training of modern neural network models is an open challenge, motivating methods that select subsets of training data while aiming to match full-data training performance.

gap.claim: Memorization scores can identify representative and atypical samples but are notably resource-intensive to compute.

contributions.claim: A memorization-score proxy based on the discrepancy between sharpness-aware minimization and stochastic gradient descent is proposed to capture atypical data points.
The proposed metric is evaluated over several efficient approximation functions for memorization scores, showing correlation and effectiveness.
The work examines approximation quality by relating typical data points to flatter loss landscapes than atypical data points.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their method as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Memorization-aware dataset summarization improves subset construction performance.
The evaluated proxy shows superior correlation and effectiveness across several efficient approximation functions.
Extensive experiments report that the proxy surpasses state-of-the-art approaches in canonical dataset-pruning and summarization setups and in few-shot learning scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sustainable neural-network training is presented as an open challenge, and subset-based training is described as an existing strategy.
Memorization scores are explored for identifying representative and atypical samples, but their computation is resource-intensive.
A proxy using the discrepancy between sharpness-aware minimization and stochastic gradient descent is proposed to capture atypicality.
Approximation functions are evaluated, and the relationship between atypicality and loss-surface flatness is examined.
Experiments report effectiveness for pruning and summarization, including canonical and few-shot settings with differing effects of atypical points.

source_observation.claim: A discrepancy between sharpness-aware minimization and stochastic gradient descent is used as a proxy for data-point atypicality.

interpretation.claim: Loss-surface geometry may provide a less resource-intensive route to approximating memorization-related signals.

application.claim: Use geometry-based memorization proxies when constructing datasets for pruning or summarization.

exception.claim: The reported role of atypical data depends on the setting: atypical points benefit canonical setups but can be detrimental in few-shot learning.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, model architectures, training budgets, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not define the proxy formula or the evaluated approximation functions.
The abstract does not quantify the reported correlations, effectiveness gains, or state-of-the-art margins.
